title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Schedule of Hold Lengths and Extensions
content:
**Hardship and Protective Holds** are granted for a fixed number of calendar days at the first grant, and a running hold of most tiers may be lengthened by extension. This schedule sets, for every tier, the length of the first grant and the extension figures.

## Terms used in the schedule

- **Initial hold days** — the calendar days of the first grant of the hold.
- **Maximum extensions** — the number of extensions allowed per hold, a whole number.
- **Extension days** — the calendar days one extension adds to the hold.
- **Updated documentation for an extension** — whether updated documentation is required for an extension.
- **Extension request window** — the calendar days before the hold's current end date from which an extension may be requested.
- **Extension decision time** — the business days after an extension request within which it is decided.

## Schedule

| Tier | Initial hold days | Maximum extensions | Extension days | Updated documentation for an extension | Extension request window (calendar days) | Extension decision time (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | 30 | 0 | 0 | Not required | 0 | 0 |
| Documented Hardship Hold | 60 | 1 | 30 | Required | 10 | 5 |
| Disaster Relief Hold | 90 | 1 | 60 | Required | 14 | 3 |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | 120 | 1 | 60 | Required | 14 | 5 |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | 180 | 1 | 90 | Required | 21 | 10 |
| Military Service Hold | 180 | 3 | 180 | Required | 30 | 3 |

## Reading the schedule

- The 30-Day Hardship Pause shows a maximum of 0 extensions: a pause runs its 30 days and is not lengthened by extension.
- The Military Service Hold is the only tier allowing more than one extension (3 per hold).
- Every tier other than the 30-Day Hardship Pause requires updated documentation for an extension.
- The same initial length, 180 calendar days, applies to the Long-Term Hardship Hold and the Military Service Hold; they differ in the number of extensions (1 against 3) and in the extension window (21 against 30 calendar days).

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Disaster Relief Hold whose current end date is 30 September has an extension request window of 14 calendar days before that date. Counting back 14 calendar days from 30 September gives 16 September, so a request dated 16 September is no earlier than the window allows, while a request dated 15 September is earlier than the window allows.
